# Technical Notes

## The whole content layer is generated by a Python script

Five Java files under `src/generated/java/` carry a header stating it outright:

> `// Generated by tools/generate_content.py. Do not edit by hand.`

| Generated file | Lines | Holds |
|:---|---:|:---|
| `GeneratedBlockCatalog` | **6064** | **277 `BuildingBlockDefinition` entries** |
| `GeneratedFamilies` | 207 | 18 `MaterialFamilySpec` |
| `GeneratedSpecialShapes` | 40 | 15 hand-authored collision shapes |
| `GeneratedPalette` | 37 | 23 `ColorPaletteEntry` |
| `GeneratedCollections` | 23 | 2 `ContentCollectionSpec` |

::: info
**This is the first mod in this batch to put generated *Java source* in its own source set.** Datagen producing generated *resources* is common; generating the Java that declares the content is not. `ModBlocks.java` is only 157 lines with a single `register(` call because it iterates `GeneratedBlockCatalog` instead of listing blocks.

Consequence for contributors: **editing the generated files is pointless** — the specification lives in the Python tool, and the next run overwrites them.
:::

## Resource scale

| Resource | main | generated | total |
|:---|---:|---:|---:|
| Blockstates | 33 | 242 | **275** |
| Models | 259 | 757 | **1016** |
| Item definitions | — | 275 | **275** |
| Loot tables | — | 275 | **275** |
| Textures | 107 | — | **107** |
| Block tags | — | 1 | **1** |

Two things to read from this:

**275 blocks, 275 loot tables, 275 item definitions — the sets are identical.** I compared the loot-table and item-definition name sets directly: zero difference. **Every block drops itself and every block has an item**, so nothing in this mod can be permanently destroyed by breaking it. That is rarer in this batch than it should be.

**107 textures produce 1016 models.** The ratio is the point of the family/palette design: one tile texture per colour, reused across six shapes.

## Localization is complete

| File | Keys |
|:---|---:|
| `en_us.json` | **556** |
| `zh_cn.json` | **556** |

**Both files have exactly 556 keys.** Every colour and family in the spec carries both a Chinese and an English display name (`"小方砖", "Small Tile"`), which is why the counts match rather than one language trailing. This is among the best-localized mods in the batch.

## What is deliberately absent

**No recipes.** No `recipe/` directory exists anywhere in the mod. All 275 blocks are creative-tab or `/give` only. See [Getting started](01_getting_started).

**No configuration.** `Config.java` exists but declares **zero options** and is **never registered** — no `registerConfig` call. Nothing appears in `config/`. Nothing about the mod is tunable, which for a pure building-block set is a reasonable choice rather than an oversight.

**No commands, no block entities, no menus, no entities, no sounds beyond block defaults.**

**No dependencies.** `neoforge.mods.toml` declares only `neoforge` and `minecraft` — genuinely standalone, unlike most of this batch.

## Metadata

| Field | Value |
|:---|:---|
| Mod id | `mirage2004` (toml uses `${mod_id}`, so gradle's value applies — four-way consistent) |
| Version | `0.1.0` |
| License | MIT |
| Minecraft | `[26.1.2]` — single exact version |
| NeoForge | 26.1.2.73 |
| Java package | `net.littlebai.mirage2004` |

The mod is at version `0.1.0` and the catalogue is already 275 blocks — the generator is doing the work that a version number this early would not otherwise support.
